## Purpose

Prepare a shared dataset that fits your team's statistical stories. Document
how you move from the supplied data to the observations and variables you will
analyze, so teammates and a skilled analyst can reproduce those decisions.

[Project Prompt](project_1_prompt.qmd) | [Analysis Plan](project_1_analysis_plan.qmd) | [Your Section's Timeline](project_1_timeline.qmd)

## Your Role and Available Help

You are **not expected to complete every cleaning, joining, or coding task on
your own**. The instructor can help wherever needed to get the data prepared.
Your responsibility is to outline your sources and data needs in the current
`team/analysis_plan.qmd`: the story or hypothesis, observations and variables
needed, source tables or additional sources, filters, derived measures, and any
joins or coding tasks you need help with. Explain how those needs support your
analysis, even when the implementation is not yet clear.

The Analysis Plan is a **working document**. Changes since its checkpoint
submission are fine: update the same plan as your questions, hypotheses, sources,
or data needs develop. Preparation and requests for help should follow the
current plan, not be constrained to the version originally submitted.

::: {.callout-tip title="Outline the Need; Ask for Help"}
Describe what data you need and why in your current Analysis Plan. Bring that
plan and your questions to the instructor for help with preparation. You do
not need to solve a difficult join or write unfamiliar code before asking.
Document the resulting decisions and code in the preparation document,
including steps completed with assistance.
:::

## Files for This Milestone

These are paths inside your team's own Posit Cloud project, not links to another
team's files. Work in `team/prepare_data.qmd`. Your named clean CSV and
`team/prepare_data.pdf` will appear beside that document in `team/`.
If your template uses different names, identify the equivalent files in your
submission. Read `data/DATA_NOTES.md` for the supplied tables and scope.

## Name Your Document and Dataset

At the top of `team/prepare_data.qmd`, update the document title to identify your
group. Set `clean_file` to a CSV filename identifying your team, such as
`Group04_Traffic_clean.csv`. This is an example, not a required naming pattern.
Replace `GroupXX`, keep the `.csv` extension, and enter a filename without a
folder path. The template saves it in `team/` automatically.

## Prepare and Explain the Data

Use your current Analysis Plan to decide which observations and variables your
stories need. With instructor help wherever needed, prepare the data and explain
the decisions alongside the code:

1. Identify the source tables, time coverage, and unit of observation.
2. Select needed variables and document filters and excluded observations.
3. Explain missing-value treatment and distinguish missing values from zero.
4. Define derived variables and calculations, including units and denominators.
5. If you combine tables, identify the keys and expected relationship. Check
   unmatched records and row counts; summarize first when needed to preserve
   your intended unit of observation.
6. Check that the resulting variables and population address your hypotheses.

Keep the supplied setup and final save chunks. Add readable R chunks and
explanations between them. If you identify an additional-data gap, outline the needed
variables, sources, unit, geography, time period, and possible keys in the
current plan. The instructor or an assisting agent can help obtain and integrate
that evidence.
Record its source and limitations.

## Render and Check the Saved Dataset

Click **Render** in `team/prepare_data.qmd`. This intentionally runs import and
preparation, writes the named CSV to `team/`, and creates the preparation PDF.
Confirm that the CSV exists, has the expected rows and columns, and contains
sensible values for the variables used in your stories.

::: {.callout-important title="One Shared Dataset"}
All teammates should analyze the same saved clean CSV. Render preparation again
when its code or additional data changes. Hypothesis documents read the saved
CSV as `clean_data`; rendering them does not repeat preparation.
:::

Download that named CSV directly from `team/` to use in Excel or Tableau.
Record how each final external-tool chart, table, or descriptive finding was
made in `team/descriptive_evidence.qmd`: source file, filters, calculations,
grouping, and relevant visual choices. A skilled analyst should be able to
recreate the final evidence from the notes; screenshots and click-by-click
instructions are not required.

## Submission

Submit in **Clean Dataset** in Canvas by the deadline on your section's
timeline. One teammate may submit for the team; include the group number and
teammate names. Upload the clean CSV or identify its location in the team
project as directed in the assignment. Include the exact CSV filename, the
Posit Cloud project link when identifying its location, and
`team/prepare_data.qmd` as the preparation source. The preparation PDF is useful
for reviewing the explanations; keep the editable source in the project.

This checkpoint does not require separately submitting each teammate's
hypothesis document. Your final Technical Documentation will assemble the
preparation explanation and code with the completed analyses.

## Checklist

- [ ] The document title and clean CSV filename identify the team.
- [ ] The current Analysis Plan outlines the sources, data needs, and tasks needing help.
- [ ] Preparation decisions connect to the current stories and hypotheses.
- [ ] Filters, missing values, derived variables, and any joins are documented.
- [ ] The preparation document renders and the saved CSV passes basic checks.
- [ ] Teammates know which CSV to use and where to find it in `team/`.
- [ ] The submission identifies the dataset and preparation source.

## Grading Basis

This is the preparation checkpoint described in the [Project Prompt](project_1_prompt.qmd).
That prompt defines the existing prep-work policy; the section timeline defines
the deadline.
